title: Licences and permits a business needs after registration
summary: What a business in Mauritius needs beyond registration: the Building and Land Use Permit from the council, the yearly trade fee, the National Electronic Licensing System, and the main sector licences with the bodies that issue them. Written for someone opening a first business.
audience: First-time business owners and people opening new premises in Mauritius.

facts.label: Building and Land Use Permit: time for a decision
facts.detail: Counted from the effective date of the application. 3 working days for a micro or small enterprise registered under the Small and Medium Enterprises Act 2017. Text of the Act as at 13 October 2025.

facts.label: Building and Land Use Permit: application fee
facts.detail: A fee set by each council is payable when the permit is issued.

facts.label: Trade fee due dates, financial year 2026/2027
facts.detail: First instalment, for 1 July to 31 December 2026, by 20 January 2027. Second instalment, for 1 January to 30 June 2027, by 30 June 2027. Paid at the Corporate and Business Registration Department.

facts.label: Surcharge on a late trade fee
facts.detail: On any amount not paid within the period set by section 122 of the Local Government Act.

facts.label: Small trade fees
facts.value: Not payable where the annual fee is MUR 5,000 or less
facts.detail: Section 122(6B): for 11 years from 1 January 2017, for an operator whose annual trade fee did not exceed MUR 5,000 at 30 June 2016. Not for trades under the Excise Act, gambling or other prescribed activities.

facts.label: Trade fee for a new business
facts.value: First payable 2 financial years after registration
facts.detail: Part of a financial year counts as one financial year. Applies to businesses registered on or after 5 August 2021.

facts.label: Fire certificate fee
facts.value: MUR 1,000 for premises up to 1,000 m2
facts.detail: Plus MUR 1,000 for each additional 1,000 m2 or part, up to MUR 25,000. No application fee. Figures from the fire service guideline dated 13 September 2021.

facts.label: Food Handler's Certificate
facts.detail: Food Regulations 2024. The fee provisions were set to start on 1 September 2025.

facts.label: Liquor retail licence (off premises), year 2026
facts.detail: A processing fee of MUR 1,500 applies to an application for the issue or transfer of a Part II licence from 1 October 2025.

facts.label: Tourist Enterprise Licence
facts.detail: From the date of issue, or a shorter period set by the Tourism Authority.

sections.heading: What sits on top of registration

blocks.text: Registering a business or incorporating a company does not by itself allow every activity to start. Three further layers can apply: a Building and Land Use Permit for the premises, an annual trade fee for a classified trade, and a licence, certificate or approval from the body that regulates the sector.

The Local Government Act makes each Municipal City Council, Municipal Town Council or District Council responsible for the Building and Land Use Permit in its area. A classified trade is a business listed in the Twelfth Schedule to that Act. The Corporate and Business Registration Department publishes the list of classified trades and the trade fee for each one.

blocks.text: The table above is the registry's own list of regulated activities that require approval by the relevant authorities. It is not a full list of sector licences. The table later in this guide covers more sectors.

No development works may be undertaken unless a Building and Land Use Permit has been issued for them. Development works include putting up, extending or demolishing a building, altering or repairing a building, making a material change in the use of a building or of land around it, and dividing land. The City Council of Port Louis lists starting up a business, changing the use of a building or plot, displaying an advertising sign and using electric engines or motors among the cases that need a permit.

items: Apply to the council for the area where the premises are, through the National Electronic Licensing System. The Act says the application must be made through that system. No application fee is payable.
The council's Chief Executive may ask for more information or documents within 8 working days of receipt. Once the application is complete it gets an effective date and an acknowledgement receipt.

The council forwards the application to the Permits and Business Monitoring Committee and, where a clearance is needed, to bodies such as the Ministry responsible for health, the Central Electricity Board, the Central Water Authority or the Waste Water Management Authority. Each has 5 working days to give its clearance. If it does not answer in time, the clearance is taken as given.

The Committee approves the application or refuses it in writing with reasons within 14 working days of the effective date. The limit is 3 working days for a micro or small enterprise registered under the Small and Medium Enterprises Act 2017.
On approval, pay the fee set by the council. The permit is then issued through the National Electronic Licensing System, with any conditions the council decides.
A refusal can be appealed to the Environment and Land Use Appeal Tribunal within 21 days of receiving the notification.

If the applicant has neither a permit nor a refusal within 2 working days after the time limit ends, the application is deemed approved once the fee is paid. The acknowledgement receipt and the fee receipt together then count as the permit. This does not apply to some cases, such as premises in the Buffer Zones or a place of public worship.
No fee is payable for the issue of a permit to build a pharmaceutical manufacturing factory, a food processing plant, a warehouse or a sheltered farming structure.

A permit granted for an economic activity states the cluster the activity belongs to. A change of activity inside the same cluster needs no fresh permit, subject to the Eleventh Schedule. A change to another cluster needs a fresh permit.

The Act does not require a permit from a person who sets up a greenhouse for crop production on agricultural land, or who carries out a classified trade that regulations exempt. The City Council of Port Louis also lists a home based activity that follows the Planning Policy Guidance as exempt.

blocks.text: Each council sets its own fee for the issue of a permit by regulations. For the documents to file, the City Council of Port Louis refers applicants to the Building and Land Use Permit Guide on the Economic Development Board's platform.

sections.heading: Trade fees under the Local Government Act

blocks.text: A person who carries out a classified trade in the area of a council pays the prescribed fee to that council. Since 1 January 2020 the fee is paid through the Registrar, which in practice means the Corporate and Business Registration Department, at its office or online. The fee for a financial year is due on 20 January. Where it is more than MUR 5,000 it may be paid in 2 equal instalments, on or before 20 January and on or before 30 June of that financial year.

columns: What the Act or the registry says
rows: First instalment, covering 1 July to 31 December 2026, payable until 20 January 2027. Second instalment, covering 1 January to 30 June 2027, payable by 30 June 2027.
Surcharge of 50 per cent on the unpaid amount.

The fee is first payable 2 financial years after the business is registered, then every financial year. Part of a financial year counts as one. The registry applies this to businesses registered on or after 5 August 2021.
Annual fee of MUR 5,000 or less

Section 122 does not apply, for 11 years from 1 January 2017, to an operator whose annual trade fee did not exceed MUR 5,000 at 30 June 2016. That period ends on 31 December 2027. The registry's notice for 2024/2025 put it this way: businesses whose fees are not more than MUR 5,000 are exempted.
It does not cover trades regulated under the Excise Act, gambling activities or other prescribed activities.
No trade fee for the holder of a certificate, licence or permit from the Tourism Authority, or for the holder of a Global Business Licence with no physical office in Mauritius.
The fee may be paid in advance for up to 3 years.

items: Find the trade and its fee in the list of classified trades and trade fees published by the Corporate and Business Registration Department.
To pay online, register with Mauritius Network Services, log in, open the section for yearly and trade fees, search the pending fees for the business registration number and choose the instalment.
To pay in person, go to the cash office of the Corporate and Business Registration Department, One Cathedral Square Building, Jules Koenig Street, Port Louis.
The Registrar remits the fees and any surcharge collected to the council concerned.

blocks.text: From 1 August 2026 trade fees for three trade codes are no longer paid at the Corporate and Business Registration Department: 70100 Agent in Land and/or Building or Estate Agent, 70101 Multipurpose Hall and 70200 Land Promoter and Property Developer. The registry directs these payments to the Real Estate Agent Authority. Its earlier notice says the two exemptions above do not apply to these activities.

The National Electronic Licensing System, often written NELS, is run by the Economic Development Board at business.edbmauritius.org. The Board describes it as a single entry point for the application, payment, processing and determination of business-related licences. The site calls itself the Mauritius Business Licensing Platform.

items: The sequence below is the one the fire service describes for its certificate. Register an account on the platform.
Choose the permit, fill in the online form and upload the documents asked for.
Answer any request for clarification and follow the status of the application online. The system sends alerts by SMS and email.
Pay the fee when the application is approved, online by credit card or with a payment voucher at the body's cash office.

blocks.text: The Tourist Enterprise Licence, the Food Handler's Certificate, the private security licence and trade fees were not listed on the platform on 20 November 2026. They are handled by the bodies named in this guide.

A fire certificate is required under section 19 of the Mauritius Fire and Rescue Service Act 2013 and the Fire Safety Plan and Fire Certificate Regulations 2018, as amended in 2021. Since 13 September 2021 every application and renewal is filed on the National Electronic Licensing System. A certificate is valid for at least one year and at most 3 years, depending on the risk assessment of the premises.

items: Commercial premises.

Any other premises to which the public has access.

items: The owner of the premises applies. Where there is a single occupier, the occupier may apply with the owner's written consent and a letter undertaking to carry out the fire safety requirements. Where the premises have several owners, a syndic applies.
The fire service checks the application and documents. A complete application gets an effective date and lapses 6 months after it.
An officer visits the site.

If the premises meet fire safety norms, a payment voucher is issued and the certificate follows payment. If not, the applicant receives recommendations, carries out the works and pays for a reinspection.

blocks.text: The Food Act 2022 says no person may operate a food business unless registered under the Business Registration Act. A food business covers any stage of manufacture, processing, packaging, storage, transport, import or distribution of food, and includes food services, catering and the sale of food.

items: Every person engaged in the sale, preparation, manufacture, serving, packing, cooking, carriage, handling or delivery of food for sale must hold a valid Food Handler's Certificate at all times.
No person may employ in a food business anyone who does not hold a valid certificate.

The certificate states that the holder has had a medical examination by a Government Medical Officer, has no infectious or communicable disease, is fit to work in a food establishment and has followed an approved food safety and hygiene training course.
The application goes to the supervising officer of the Ministry of Health and Wellness. The certificate is valid for 3 years and may be renewed for further periods of 3 years.
The fee for issue or renewal is MUR 300. A duplicate costs MUR 100.
A renewal application is due at least 30 days before expiry. A later application carries a surcharge of 50 per cent.

blocks.text: No person may import, manufacture or sell a food listed in the Second Schedule to the Food Regulations 2024 without a pre-market approval permit from the supervising officer. The application is made through TradeNet or on the form in the regulations, with a certificate of analysis from an accredited laboratory. The fee is MUR 5,000 for each approval granted. The fee for verification of imported food and clearance to Customs is MUR 1,000 for each clearance.

The Food Regulations 2024 came into operation on 9 September 2024 and replaced the Food Regulations 1999. Their fee provisions were first set to start on 1 March 2025 and were moved to 1 September 2025 by Government Notice No. 19 of 2025. A ministry notice of 21 January 2016, still linked from its Food Handler's Certificate page, gives a validity of two years. The 2024 regulations are the later text and give 3 years.

sections.heading: Environment licences and import and export permits

blocks.text: Under the Environment Act 2024 no proponent may start, alter or modify an undertaking listed in Part A of the Sixth Schedule without a Preliminary Environmental Report (PER) licence, or one listed in Part B without an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) licence. Part C lists undertakings that need a Strategic Environmental Assessment licence. Doing so without the licence is an offence. A project that is not listed is treated as an undertaking by the Minister where its nature, scope, scale and sensitive location make it likely to affect the environment or the zoning of an area.

items: Part A, PER licence, includes for example: manufacture of animal feed, manufacture of paint, manufacture of plastic products involving melting, moulding and extrusion, a ready-mix concrete plant, rearing of poultry above 15,000 heads, a recycling plant, a sawmill, a slaughter house and a textile industry associated with washing, bleaching and printing.
Part B, EIA licence, includes for example an asphalt plant, a landfill, the manufacture of batteries and land clearing and development in or on environmentally sensitive areas.
A Building and Land Use Permit for a scheduled undertaking is approved only where there is an approved preliminary environmental report or an EIA licence.

PER approval and the EIA licence are applied for on the National Electronic Licensing System. A ministry notice of 6 November 2026 says the Completion Certificate for PER, EIA and SEA projects is now applied for there too, with 2 hard copies sent to the Ministry.

blocks.text: Controlled goods may enter Mauritius only with an import permit or an authorisation from the relevant authority. Without it the goods are detained and referred to that authority. Prohibited goods cannot be imported, exported, transited, sold or circulated. The official trade portal says an import permit or an approval to clear controlled goods is normally issued within 3 working days when all information and documents have been supplied.

items: The Mauritius Revenue Authority lists prohibited and restricted imports under the Consumer Protection (Control of Imports) Regulations 2017.

Foodstuffs need permits from health or agricultural authorities. Plants and plant products need clearance from the Ministry of Agro Industry and Food Security. Weights and balances need authorisation from the Legal Metrology Services. Pharmaceutical products need authorisation from the Government Pharmacist.
If the authority refuses a permit, the imported goods are liable to seizure.

Most goods can be exported freely. A few controlled items need an export permit before export. The trade portal says export permits and export certificates are approved and delivered on the same day through TradeNet when all conditions are met, and Kimberley Process Certificates within 2 working days.

blocks.text: No person may carry on a business listed in the Second Schedule to the Excise Act without the matching licence. The licensing authority is the Director-General of the Mauritius Revenue Authority. An application for a Part I or Part II licence needs a certificate of character issued by the Director of Public Prosecutions. An application for a Part III licence needs a clearance from the Commissioner of Police. Part I and Part II licences expire on 31 December. A licence renewed more than 14 days after expiry attracts a surcharge of 50 per cent. A licensee may not sell alcohol to a person under 18.

Holders of the hotel and guest house, restaurant, private club, night club, pub and table d'hôte licences must hold a valid Tourist Enterprise Licence or Tourist Accommodation Certificate when they renew.
A wholesale dealer must have furnished security by means of a bond to the Mauritius Revenue Authority.

Part I lists manufacturing licences. Examples: manufacturer of cigarettes and other tobacco products MUR 10,000 a year, brewer MUR 20,000, bottler of water MUR 500, importer or manufacturer of sugar sweetened products MUR 500.

blocks.text: Tourism. A Tourist Enterprise Licence is issued for an establishment or activity run to provide services or goods to tourists for reward. The Tourism Authority publishes a checklist for each type, including restaurant, pub, night club, private club, table d'hôte, spa, golf course, karting, eco tourism, tour operator, travel agency, online travel agency, rental agencies for bicycles, motorcycles, quads and buses, and tourist guide. Renewal is applied for within 3 months before expiry. A renewal made within 30 days after expiry carries a surcharge of 50 per cent, and the licence lapses if it is not renewed within those 30 days. The Tourist Accommodation Certificate covers hotels, guest houses, tourist residences and domaines and is valid for 3 consecutive years. An Act gazetted on 13 August 2026 added an outdoor accommodation certificate and a temporary tourist accommodation certificate valid for up to 90 days.

Construction. The Construction Industry Authority Act 2023 repealed the Construction Industry Development Board Act. The assets of the former Board vested in the Construction Industry Authority, and registration certificates issued by the Board that were still valid are deemed issued by the Authority. The Local Government Act records the changes made by the 2023 Act as in force from 1 April 2024. Under the 2023 Act no local contractor may undertake construction works unless registered under the Act and unless, where one is needed, there is a valid Building and Land Use Permit for the works. No local consultant may provide consultancy services unless registered. Importers, manufacturers and producers of listed construction materials, plant and equipment register as suppliers. A contractor's or consultant's registration runs to the next 30 June and is renewable yearly. The renewal application is due at least one month before expiry. A renewal within 30 days after expiry carries a surcharge of 25 per cent, and the registration lapses after those 30 days.

Private security and pharmacies. A Private Security Service Provider Licence is applied for by appointment at the Police Prosecution Office, Private Security Section, Sterling House, Port Louis, under the Private Security Service Act 2004. The licence costs MUR 10,000, is valid for one year and must be renewed not later than 21 days before expiry. The documents include a development permit from the council stating that the place is to be used by a private security service provider. Under the Pharmacy Act no person may operate a pharmacy without a licence from the Pharmacy Board and a pharmacist in charge. The Board has the premises inspected and takes account of the number of pharmacies in the area. The licence is valid for one year and is renewed each year.
